questions.question: You create a public DNS zone named contoso.com in Azure DNS and add records. Internet users still receive answers from the previous DNS provider. What should you do?

options.text: Update the NS records at the domain registrar to the name servers of the Azure DNS zone
options.why: Correct. Delegation tells the internet which name servers answer for the domain.

options.text: Add an SOA record to the zone
options.why: Azure DNS creates the SOA record automatically.

options.text: Link the zone to a virtual network
options.why: Virtual network links apply to private DNS zones.

options.text: Create a CNAME record at the zone apex
options.why: CNAME records are not allowed at the zone apex, and they do not delegate the domain.

questions.explanation: To delegate a domain to Azure DNS, configure the four Azure DNS name servers as the NS records at the registrar or parent zone.

questions.question: The zone apex contoso.com must resolve to the public IP address of a load balancer. The record must update automatically if the IP address changes. What should you create?

options.text: An alias A record set at @ that references the public IP address resource
options.why: Correct. Alias records reference the Azure resource and can be used at the apex.

options.text: A CNAME record at @
options.why: CNAME records are not allowed at the zone apex.

options.text: An A record at @ that contains the current IP address
options.why: A static A record does not update when the IP address changes.

options.text: A TXT record at @
options.why: TXT records do not resolve to IP addresses.

questions.explanation: Alias records point to Azure resources such as public IPs, Traffic Manager profiles and Front Door, and follow changes to the resource.

questions.question: A private DNS zone named contoso.internal is linked to VNet1 with auto-registration enabled. VNet2 is peered with VNet1. VMs in VNet2 cannot resolve names in contoso.internal. What should you do?

options.text: Create a virtual network link from contoso.internal to VNet2
options.why: Correct. Each virtual network that resolves the zone needs its own link.

options.text: Enable gateway transit on the peering
options.why: Gateway transit shares a VPN gateway and does not share DNS zones.

options.text: Create a public DNS zone named contoso.internal
options.why: A public zone answers internet queries, not private ones.

options.text: Enable auto-registration on VNet1 again
options.why: Auto-registration is already enabled and does not affect VNet2.

questions.explanation: Peering does not share private DNS zones. Link the zone to every virtual network that needs to resolve it.

questions.question: You need the names of VMs in VNet1 to be added to and removed from a private DNS zone automatically. VNet1 already has auto-registration enabled for a private zone named corp.internal. What happens if you link VNet1 to a second private zone named apps.internal with auto-registration enabled?

options.text: The operation fails because a virtual network can have only one registration zone
options.why: Correct. VNet1 can be linked to apps.internal for resolution only.

options.text: VM records are registered in both zones
options.why: A virtual network supports only one registration zone.

options.text: The registration moves from corp.internal to apps.internal
options.why: Azure does not move registration automatically.

options.text: The link is created, but VMs are registered only after a restart
options.why: The link with registration enabled cannot be created.

questions.explanation: Each virtual network can have one private DNS zone with auto-registration, and resolution links to additional zones.

questions.question: Which two record types can you create as alias record sets in an Azure public DNS zone? Each correct answer presents a complete solution.

options.text: A
options.why: Correct. Alias A records can reference public IP addresses and other resources.

options.text: CNAME
options.why: Correct. Alias CNAME records can reference resources such as Traffic Manager.

options.text: MX
options.why: MX records cannot be alias records.

options.text: SRV
options.why: SRV records cannot be alias records.

questions.explanation: Azure DNS supports alias record sets for A, AAAA and CNAME records.
